description: Canonical test vectors for the SEP-XXXX Soroban contract (`contracts/sep-xxxx`). Pinned by the design spec — every value here is derivable from `contracts/sep-xxxx/src/lib.rs` (current testnet contract) or `docs/democracy-update-testnet-design.md` (v2 redeploy planned in Phase C). Vectors that depend on Poseidon / Groth16 outputs are deliberately omitted: those are produced by Phase A's `prove_democracy_v2` reference implementation and added to `docs/cross-platform-test-vectors.json` per §6 step A6. The vectors below cover the contract surface only — error codes, enum values, validation boundaries, wire shapes, dispatch routing, and bitmap-to-field-element packing rules — i.e., the parts that any conforming contract reimplementation MUST match byte-for-byte without running cryptography.

error_codes.description: Numeric values of `Error` variants (`#[contracterror] #[repr(u32)]`). The contract's ABI and every client-side error mapping MUST agree on these. New entries introduced by the v2 design are flagged `since="v2"`.

vectors.name: Reserved3
vectors.note: previously Unauthorized; admin checks now use require_auth() which panics

vectors.name: MemberCountMismatch
vectors.note: v1-only — removed in v2 (no member_count in storage)

vectors.name: MemberCountOutOfRange
vectors.note: v1-only — removed in v2 (count constraints internalised in circuit)

vectors.name: GroupTypeMismatch
vectors.note: polymorphic update_commitment rejects when claimed_group_type in UpdateCommitmentPublicInputs ≠ stored.group_type (§4.7.4 type-confusion guard)

group_type_enum.description: `group_type` u32 values stored in `CommitmentEntryV2.group_type`. Same numeric ABI in v1 and v2.

tier.description: Tier index → tree depth → leaf capacity. `tier_capacity()` returns 0 for any out-of-range tier; the contract MUST reject `tier > 2` with `InvalidTier` before reaching `tier_capacity`. v2 keeps this mapping unchanged.

vk_kind_enum.description: Discriminator values for the `VkKind` enum (passed to `update_vk`). The numeric ordering matches the variant declaration order in `lib.rs`. `UpdateByType(u32)` carries the group_type as an associated u32; only group_type=2 (Democracy) is an installable VK family in v2 testnet (Oligarchy=3 lands later per §11).

vectors.name: UpdateByType(2)
vectors.note: v2 swaps the two count IC points for two occupancy_commitment IC points and adds threshold_numerator (§4.7.3 step 5, §4.7.6). Wire-supplied inputs in v2 are 5 scalars; threshold_numerator is supplied by the contract from storage at verify time, not by the caller.

create_group_v2_validation.description: Per-group_type validation in `create_group_v2` (v1 contract — the entrypoint kept for Anarchy/1v1 on the testnet contract). v2 supersedes this with `create_group_v3` for Democracy + Oligarchy; Anarchy continues to use `create_group_v2`.

vectors.name: Anarchy
rules: member_count is informational; any value ≤ tier_capacity(tier) accepted (the contract does not bound it for Anarchy in current source — note: the source reads `if member_count > tier_capacity(tier) { Err(MemberCountOutOfRange) }` only inside the Democracy arm; Anarchy accepts any u32. Reimplementations MUST match.)

vectors.name: Democracy (v1 contract)
rules: member_count ∈ [0, tier_capacity(tier)]; any out-of-range value yields MemberCountOutOfRange
member_count == 0 and == 1 are accepted at create time (group grows via off-chain MLS); democracy-of-≥2 invariant is enforced at first update_commitment_democracy call

vectors.name: Oligarchy
rules: create_group_v2 rejects with UnknownGroupType — Oligarchy uses the separate create_oligarchy_group entrypoint that takes admin_root

create_group_v3_validation.description: New entrypoint introduced in §6 step C1 for the v2 contract redeploy. Replaces both create_group_v2 (for Democracy) and create_oligarchy_group (when Oligarchy lands per §11). Carries threshold_numerator for Democracy (§4.7.6) and the initial occupancy_commitment for the creator-only state.

threshold_numerator_validation.rule: threshold_numerator MUST be in [1, 100] for Democracy groups; MUST be ignored (or set to 0 sentinel — implementer's choice, but consistent across the codebase) for non-Democracy groups

update_commitment_polymorphic_dispatch.description: v2's polymorphic `update_commitment` entrypoint dispatches on `current.group_type` (read from storage) to the matching update VK family. The discriminator on `UpdateCommitmentPublicInputs` MUST equal `current.group_type`; mismatch is rejected with `GroupTypeMismatch` BEFORE proof verification (no chain-pairing wasted on a type-confusion attempt). See §4.7.4.

vectors.name: OneOnOne
vectors.note: 1v1 groups are immutable; update_commitment rejects regardless of public-inputs variant

vectors.name: Oligarchy
vectors.expected_vk_kind: UpdateByType(3) (tier-indexed; IC count TBD by Oligarchy circuit design)
vectors.note: Oligarchy update_commitment dispatch lands per §11 follow-up; the dispatch arm is the placeholder that reserves the slot.

type_confusion_guard.description: The discriminator inside the wire-supplied UpdateCommitmentPublicInputs MUST match the stored group_type. Mismatch is rejected BEFORE any cryptographic check.

domain_tags.description: Field-element domain tags used inside Poseidon hash inputs. Pinned per §10.1 (Phase-A blocker). Codified in the planned `src/circuit/domain_tags.rs`. Future circuits MUST NOT reuse these values.

occupancy_bitmap_fold.description: Per §4.7.2, the occupancy bitmap is folded into Fr scalar field elements at BITS_PER_FELT = 252 bits per scalar. Each scalar packs 252 bitmap bits in little-endian order: bit i of the bitmap is bit (i mod 252) of scalar (i div 252). The high (255-th, 254-th, 253-rd, 252-th) bits of every scalar MUST be zero — this keeps the encoding canonical (Fr modulus is ~2^254.86, so the high 3 bits cannot all be 1). Vectors below specify the bit→(scalar_index, bit_offset) mapping rule and the per-tier scalar count; concrete Poseidon hash outputs are deferred to the cross-platform vectors file populated by Phase A6.

scalar_count_by_tier.note: 256 bits = ceil(256/252) = 2 scalars; 4 high bits of scalar 1 are zero-padded
2048 bits = ceil(2048/252) = 9 scalars; 220 high bits of scalar 8 are zero-padded

occupancy_bitmap_fold.bit_packing_rule: bitmap[i] occupies bit position (i mod 252) of scalar (i div 252), little-endian within the scalar. Bits 252–255 of every produced scalar MUST be 0.

tier_0_examples.description: All slots empty (creator-only state has not yet been initialised; pre-creation reference)
Slot 0 active (creator-only state at create_group_v3 time)
Slots 0 and 1 active (after first member join, no tombstones)
Slots 0, 1, 3 active; slot 2 tombstoned (slot 2 was once a member, then removed)

tier_1_examples.description: Slot 252 active (first bit of scalar 1; the boundary case that wedges if BITS_PER_FELT is misimplemented as 256)
Slots 0 and 252 active (one bit per scalar; tests the cross-scalar boundary)
Slot 255 active (last bit of bitmap; bit position 3 of scalar 1)

tier_2_examples.description: Slot 2047 active (last bit of bitmap; bit position (2047 mod 252) = 31 of scalar 8)
tier_2_examples.note: Scalars 0..7 are all-zero in this single-bit example.

high_bits_zero_assertion.description: Every produced scalar MUST have bits 252–255 equal to 0 (canonical-Fr requirement). Implementations MUST reject (or refuse to produce) any scalar where the top byte (BE) has any of the high 4 bits set.

membership_count_validation_v2.description: v2 internalises the count-derived rules into the circuit (§4.7.3 step 3). The contract no longer reads `member_count` from storage on the update path. The values below describe what the circuit is required to enforce, expressed as bitmap popcount conditions; they are reproduced as test vectors so the C2 contract integration tests (§7.1's `prove_democracy_v2_*` cases) and the Phase A R1CS soundness review have a single source of truth.

popcount_constraints.rationale: preserves democracy-of-≥2 invariant; was contract-only in v1, now in-circuit
matches the single-signer-subset proof shape from §4.2; multi-signer transitions are deferred to Phase F
implicit in the bitmap's fixed length; no explicit constraint required
configurable per group (§4.7.6); K is the number of signers in the proof. K=1 is the single-signer subset baseline (§4.2)

single_signer_examples.note: single-signer subset hits the limit at popcount_old ≥ 3; Phase F covers larger groups

update_commitment_public_inputs_wire_for.description: Discriminated-union encoding of `UpdateCommitmentPublicInputs` for the polymorphic v2 entrypoint. Encoded as a Soroban contract enum (`#[contracttype]`) with one variant per governance type. The discriminator is a single u32 tag matching the group_type values from `group_type_enum`. Fields below give the per-variant scalar layout that feeds the Groth16 verifier (after the contract reads its own additions like threshold_numerator from storage).

variants.name: Democracy
groth16_public_inputs: threshold_numerator (supplied by contract from current.threshold_numerator; NOT on the wire)

variants.name: Oligarchy
variants.status: reserved (lands per §11 follow-up); shape determined by the Oligarchy circuit design

canonical_encoding_rules: Every BytesN<32> commitment field MUST round-trip through Fr::from_bytes ∘ Fr::to_bytes; non-canonical encodings are rejected with InvalidCommitmentEncoding (matches v1 update_commitment).
u64 epoch_old uses Soroban's native big-endian XDR encoding; it is bound to the proof via the IC[2] = epoch_old layout.
The discriminator tag is part of the wire (Soroban enum encoding); a wire that decodes to a different variant than the stored group_type is rejected with GroupTypeMismatch BEFORE proof verification.

storage_layout_v2.description: Storage entries written by the v2 contract. Replaces `CommitmentEntryV2.member_count: u32` with `occupancy_commitment: BytesN<32>` and adds `threshold_numerator: u8`. Existing v1 keys (`Group`, `History`, `GroupV2`, `HistoryV2`) are unused by v2 — the v2 contract is a fresh deployment per §4.6, so there are no live v1 records to migrate.

fields.name: occupancy_commitment
fields.note: Poseidon hash of the slot bitmap; replaces v1's member_count

fields.name: threshold_numerator
fields.constraints: 0 for non-Democracy groups; 1..=100 for Democracy groups
fields.note: fixed at create_group_v3, never mutated thereafter (§4.7.6)

removed_in_v2.rationale: exposed via contract storage was the §3.4 leak; v2 commits to bitmap via occupancy_commitment instead

data_keys_v2_additions.name: GroupV3(BytesN<32>)
data_keys_v2_additions.note: v2-specific persistent storage key; analogous to v1's GroupV2

data_keys_v2_additions.name: HistoryV3(BytesN<32>)
data_keys_v2_additions.note: see §4.7's note that history records intentionally drop fields not needed for historical queries; the exact V3-history shape is decided in C1

epoch_invariant.description: v2 keeps v1's monotonic-by-1 epoch rule. update_commitment increments stored.epoch by exactly 1 on success.

proof_replay_protection.description: Global nullifier scope — same in v1 and v2. The nullifier is sha256(proof.a || proof.b || proof.c) over the 384-byte uncompressed proof bytes. Scope is global: the same 384 bytes used at any state-changing entrypoint on any group consume the nullifier. See `lib.rs` `proof_hash`.
rules: Once a proof's bytes have been recorded by record_proof, any subsequent entrypoint call with byte-identical proof.a||proof.b||proof.c is rejected with ProofReplay.

TTL of UsedProof entries is LEDGER_BUMP (~30 days). After expiry the same proof bytes can be re-used; long-lived groups require periodic state advancement to keep nullifiers alive (mitigated in part by bump_group_ttl).

Pre-inclusion mempool replay is NOT closed by the contract-level nullifier — see the long comment in `lib.rs` for what circuit-level v2 (different v2 — operation tag binding) would close that this `lib.rs`-level v2 redeploy does not.
